title: Accessibility and responsive acceptance
bodyMarkdown:
## Check a task with keyboard and the intended viewport

1. Choose a specific route, persona/state, theme and target viewport. Record the source revision and task, rather than claiming all devices from one screenshot.
2. Navigate to the intended labelled control by keyboard. Check visible focus, activation, dialog entry/exit, tab navigation and return focus. Workbench inspector tabs have focused ArrowRight evidence; verify other interactions independently.
3. Resize through the required mobile/tablet/foldable/desktop layouts and inspect text, controls, overflow and reading order. Check both themes and zoom/reflow where applicable.
4. For help/search, check the labelled query control, result count announcements, keyboard result navigation and article focus. Exercise no-results, missing article and recoverable error states while retaining an editor draft.
5. Record failures with a synthetic task and exact viewport/theme/state. A labelled DOM element is useful evidence, not proof of usable screen-reader behavior; test the intended assistive technology separately.

Historical frontend evidence covers scoped 390×700 no-overflow checks, labels/dialogs/tabs and specific editing actions. The correction packet adds its own scoped mobile/theme and Undo observations. No full screen-reader or assistive-device certification is established. Schema reachability/scalar edit counts do not prove accessibility or every provider combination.

Phone reachability through authenticated Termux forwarding is operator-reported; no automated physical-device test is recorded and does not transfer browser-local storage between devices. Use the currently authorized preview and existing owner; this guide does not open ports or create a tunnel/service.
capabilityStatus: The preview has focused layout, label and tab-interaction evidence. Complete keyboard, screen-reader and device coverage still requires testing the intended task and environment.
